dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

David is at risk due to behavioral concerns. David has shown a concerning level of resource guarding and leash biting during an incident with staff. He intially was fearful of interaction with staff, growling with a stiff body. As his stay progressed, David has been social with familiar handlers and staff. He enjoys chasing balls, plush toys, and enrichment games. During a recent incident, David began leash biting after being re-leashed to exit the play yard and return to the kennel. After grabbing the lead, he would growl at staff while guarding the leashes he was holding. Other staff attempted to assist, but David continued to guard the leashes and would lunge, growl, and snap at leads and handlers. Due to his intensity, it took several handlers to successfully remove the leads and secure him in his kennel. Medically, David is obese, has moderate-to-severe dental disease, is brachycephalic, and has anemia.

David was surrendered into care as a stray, so his past behavior in a home environment is unknown. David has not acclimated well to the shelter environment. During his medical exam, he was initially loose-bodied and solicited attention, though he began to bark, growl, and head whip when staff started to handle him. He intially was not able to undergo a handling assessment due to moving away, tensing, and growling. David has warmed up and has been social with staff and handlers as his stay has progressed. He has shown guarding behaviors with toys and leashes. David did escalate towards handlers when trying to retrieve leashes that he was guarding during an incident. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: We tend to think he's more of a Goliath than a David, but nonetheless we don't think he'll have any problem taking a giant since he is one himself. Clocking in at 95 pounds, David is just a big, mushy, ball of love. The police were alerted to David when he was tied up in Brooklyn and left abandoned. We quickly see what they might have been referring to by "stubborn" when he demands treats the whole way out of he building and back in to keep him motivated to walk. Clearly a sign of his intelligence more than anything! But with a guy of his stature, there's probably more at play than simply being obstinate. He is overweight/obese and on the early side of seniorhood. In any case, we are immediately smitten with this tongue peeking, gentle meatball.

Since arrival, David has been uncomfortable with much handling and therefore an assessment was not conducted on him. For this reason, he is available to foster through a rescue partner. At this time, he has not had a dog greet but during time out with us he was not reactive toward other dogs and seemed to largely ignore them.
